newsitem.title: TURKEY: Kurd group says won't attack second Iraqi city.
newsitem.headline: Kurd group says won't attack second Iraqi city.

text.p: Kurdish warlord Jalal Talabani said on Monday that his forces would not follow up the capture of Sulaimaniya, Iraq's biggest Kurdish city, with a push against Arbil, administrative centre of Iraqi Kurdistan.

"We don't have a plan now to do that, because the city is surrounded by Iraqi tanks," Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) leader Talabani said in an interview with the London-based Arabic newspaper al-Hayat.
"We leave Arbil to its people," he said. Talabani said the Iraqi army "intervened today (Sunday) by launching artillery shelling on Chamchamal, then it stopped."
U.N. officials and guards in Iraqi Kurdistan said on Monday that Talabani's forces had regained control of most of the territory they lost to the rival KDP of Massoud Barzani six weeks ago.
They said Talabani's guerrillas had now recaptured two more towns, Degala and Koi Sanjaq, after taking control over the strategic Dokan Dam area, site of a major hydroelectirc power project.
Iraqi government troops and tanks helped Talabani's rival Barzani take Arbil in late August, prompting U.S. missile strikes on targets in southern Iraq.
The city was home to a power-sharing regional government that fell apart in feuding between the Kurdish militias.
Talabani reiterated PUK denials that Iran helped it retake Sulaimaniya, the region's most populous city, from Barzani's Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) on Sunday.
"We urge the allied forces to intervene to confront any attack on the people of Kurdistan, let them confront any Iranian force if found in the region and any Iraqi force."
A U.S-led allied air force based in Turkey ostensibly protects Iraq's Kurds from any attack by Baghdad but it has stayed out of inter-Kurdish fighting.
The United States opposes involvement in the area by Baghdad or Tehran. Iraqi Kurdish sources said a KDP delegation was due in Turkey on Monday on its way for talks in Washington.
Talabani said 10,000 of his fighters were in control of Sulaimaniya by Saturday night. He said his guerrillas counted 364 KDP bodies but only a "small number" of PUK men were killed.
Baghdad has urged the rival Kurdish groups to stay away from outside powers, in an apparent reference to Iran.
President Saddam Hussein chaired a meeting of the Revolutionary Command Council and leaders of the ruling Baath Party on Sunday to discuss developments in the north.
The official Iraqi News Agency (INA), quoting a spokesman for the meeting, said Iraqi leaders urged the warring Kurdish factions to halt fighting and resume peace talks with Baghdad.
"We call on the parties which have resumed fighting to keep away the foreign powers and not deal with them. We also call on them to start talks between themselves.

"The leadership is ready to extend an invitation to all parties regardless of their background and our opinion or evaluation of this faction or the other, for dialogue in Baghdad, under the sponsorship of the state," INA said.
Talabani's group said in a statement on Monday that its fighters had defeated Barzani's group in clashes that followed the recapture of Sulaimaniya, in KDP hands for a month.
"Iraqi-backed Barzani militia were routed yesterday from the district of Koy Sinjak, Qala Diza, Ranya, Chwar Korna, Chamchamal and Taq Taq," the PUK said in a statement.
U.N. sources in Baghdad confirmed that the PUK forces regained control of Chamchamal, to the south of Sulaimaniya, and Darbandikhan to the east.
